subject: PICTURE clause
notes: `if (sig.IsZero) return RenderFloat(m, negative: false, new string('0', m.SigDigits), 0)` yields all-zero significand digit positions, all-zero exponent digit positions and a positive sign on both; the underflow path (a value nearer to zero than the mask can hold) returns the same rule-8 image rather than a saturated one. Probe p4 at --std 2023: PIC +9.9(3)E+99 MOVE 0 -> '+0.000E+00'; PIC -9.9(3)E+99 MOVE 0 -> ' 0.000E+00', the space being Table 8's rendering of the symbol '-' for a positive-or-zero value, which is what 'the sign of the significand, if present, shall be positive' means for that symbol. The exponent's sign is emitted as '+' whenever e >= 0. BLANK WHEN ZERO takes precedence and blanks the whole item (13.18.8's row, not this one).
